recommendation: Keep the core audit commit as-is. Make any future Permission import semantic, note, or example corrections in HL7/data-access-policies unless a later final work-group decision moves Permission back into the active FHIR core build.
issue_request: FHIR-43566 was an Applied/Persuasive with Modification Security issue for R6 asking for a Permission to reference an overarching Permission and for chained policies to have clear import semantics. The approved resolution added Permission.rule.import, an invariant preventing import from being mixed with local rule content, Composite Permissions notes, and examples.
initial_application: HL7/fhir PR #3248 lists FHIR-43566 and merged on 2025-03-05. Local history shows commit c1a3df664d5c79f9882ba8d15e9734a6c5caa1e0 added Permission.rule.import, the rule constraint, Composite Permissions notes, and base/composite examples under source/permission while Permission was still an active core resource; follow-up PR/build-cleanup commits added invariant tests and retained the feature.
additional_context: Commit 0e2a8a7f839d5e1a43787523daccf07d958362f3 later removed source/permission and active Permission entries from source/fhir.ini. Current core Security/history pages link Permission to the HL7 Data Access Policies IG, and that external source/package now contains Permission.rule.import, prm-1, Composite Permissions notes, and a composite example importing a base Permission. A prior combined-branch audit for FHIR-43583 records the same move-out-of-core context but did not decide FHIR-43566.
reconciliation: Published an empty external-repo audit commit on the combined branch. No core source change was made because reintroducing or editing source/permission in core would conflict with the current build scope.

related_jiras.note: A separate Permission issue already audited on the combined branch; it established the same current-state finding that Permission now belongs outside core.
Voted in the same 2025-03-03 Security WG Permission discussion, but concerns non-patient and directory access scope rather than overarching Permission imports.
